extracted.intended_audience: corporate communications / investor relations professionals, securities counsel, and press-release authors at public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and timing press releases so they satisfy Reg FD (broad-disclosure) obligations around analyst/investor calls and other selective contacts, maximizing regulatory compliance and media/market pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad simultaneous distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Material non-public information must be released through a broadly disseminated press release before (or simultaneously with) any selective disclosure (analyst call, investor meeting, briefing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release should be the vehicle that makes the information broadly available — selective channels (e.g., analyst-only briefings) cannot precede broad distribution. Timing matters: if information is disclosed selectively, the firm must immediately make it broadly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8-K filing alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Material developments triggering Item 2.02 (results) or Item 8.01 (other events) Form 8-K must be filed with the SEC concurrent with the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Form 8-K is filed at the same time as the press release when applicable (e.g., earnings/results). Coordinate legal/IR so the press release and required 8-K are simultaneous to avoid compliance gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-call release window
rubrics_metrics.description: When a press release accompanies an earnings call, the release should be issued at least 30 minutes before call start so all participants have equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue the release sufficiently ahead of the call (the page recommends a 30-minute buffer) to allow media, retail investors, and other market participants to access the information before or at the same time as call attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-distribution audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a recognized broad-distribution wire (Business Wire, PR Newswire, Globe Newswire) — direct-to-analyst email is not broadly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose widely used, traceable distribution services to ensure broad dissemination and to document distribution. Avoid relying on channels that reach only a subset (e.g., direct analyst emails) if the intent is broad disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded-call posting
rubrics_metrics.description: If selective remarks are made on a call, post the recording / transcript publicly within the same day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where remarks on a call contain material information not captured in the release, post audio/transcript promptly (same day) so those not on the call have access; this mitigates selective-disclosure concerns and evidences remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking disclosure parity
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward-looking statements made on calls should appear in the underlying press release in the same form (no 'extra' guidance available only to call attendees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure guidance and forward-looking commentary are mirrored in the press release if discussed on a call; do not provide additional or expanded forward-looking guidance exclusively to call participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality assessment trail
rubrics_metrics.description: Document why the issuer concluded an item was or was not material; the press release strategy should match the materiality call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an audit trail of materiality determinations and how they drove disclosure choices (e.g., why something was included in a press release or withheld). This supports compliance and defends against later challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-leakage protocol (embargo handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes for media briefings under Reg FD must end at the same instant as the press release goes broad — no 'exclusive head-start' for favored journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If holding embargoed briefings, ensure embargo lifts exactly when the press release is broadly distributed; do not give select journalists earlier access that would create selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release-as-canonical-disclosure (pickup-worthiness implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pickup-worthy modern earnings release is structured around the broad-distribution-first rule: the release is the canonical disclosure event; the call is supplementary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communications so the press release is the primary disclosure and calls/supplementary events do not convey new material information first; attempts to shift information to selective channels risk SEC enforcement, market sanctions, and reduced media/market pickup.
